binding_note: Nothing fails at 1 TiB/month: the included 100 Mbps at the 95th percentile is far above the sustained rate that volume needs. The rate is the only cap: above it the tunnel is limited to the purchased allowance and more bandwidth costs USD 0.20 per Mbps per month, so no constraint binds at this volume.

identity_cost.detail: Ordering is self-serve in the panel: "Pay in the panel, configure the generated tunnel details, then assign the IPv4 addresses." The payment and verification steps were not read, so a card requirement is inferred from a paid panel order rather than observed.

reliability_note: No DDoS protection on tunneled addresses and null-routing when attacked; the vendor says so plainly.
confidence_note: Prefix sizes, per-address price, tunnel protocols and 95th-percentile terms are all first-party. A probe past the included rate would show what the limit-down looks like.

notes: Cheapest per address of the providers compared: USD 1.50 per month is USD 18 per year for a /32, and the same price buys a /25. The price conflict is real and unresolved: the homepage tile says "From $1.25 / mo" and the product page says "$1.50 per IPv4 address per month" in three separate places. Every per-prefix figure on the product page is exactly 1.50 times the address count, so the homepage tile may be stale after a rise. $1.25 is not the 12-month term price, because 15 percent off 1.50 is 1.275, not 1.25. $1.25 may be a leftover campaign rate, like the page's other struck-through campaign prices, but that is unproven. The record keeps the product-page figure.

extras.wg_detail: The prefix is routed to the customer's endpoint: "Your selected public IPv4 space is delivered to your endpoint over WireGuard, GRE, GRETAP, SIT, or VXLAN" and "Choose WireGuard, GRE, GRETAP, SIT or VXLAN when configuring the service." It is a routed prefix, not a single NAT address: "The prefix is delivered to your tunnel endpoint for use on your router, server, firewall or customer-edge network."
extras.volume_stated: Not a byte quota but a rate, measured at the 95th percentile: "Included - 95th percentile 100 Mbps" in the UK and US, "Tunnel port 2 Gbps", and "Extra bandwidth: $0.20/Mbps". New Zealand includes 10 Mbps.
extras.transit_note: Prefixes are announced from the vendor's own AS47272 network.
